settings.headline: About Kestrel Valley Credit Union
settings.subtitle: Started in 1958 by twelve teachers and a grain elevator manager with $340 in a cigar box. Today 48,600 members own it, and it still answers to them.

settings.headline: A not-for-profit financial cooperative
settings.body:
Credit unions are owned by their members. Each member has one vote in board elections, whether they have $5 or $500,000 on deposit. The board is made up of volunteers elected by members.

We serve anyone who lives, works, worships or goes to school in Kestrel, Ashby or Wren counties, and their families.

settings.headline: How to join
settings.intro: Joining takes about 20 minutes at any branch.

items.title: Check that you can join
items.text: You can join if you live, work, worship or go to school in Kestrel, Ashby or Wren counties, or if a family member is already a member.

items.title: Bring a photo ID
items.text: A driver's license, state ID or passport, plus your Social Security number. Bring a parent or guardian if you are under 18.

items.title: Deposit $5
items.text: Your $5 opens a Share Savings account. It is your share of ownership, and it stays yours for as long as you are a member.

items.q: Is a credit union the same as a bank?
items.a: You can do the same things: checking, savings, loans and cards. The difference is ownership. A bank is owned by shareholders; a credit union is owned by its members and run by a volunteer board they elect.

items.q: Can I stay a member if I move away?
items.a: Yes. Once a member, always a member, as long as you keep your Share Savings account open.

items.q: Is this a real credit union?
items.a: No. Kestrel Valley Credit Union is fictional. It was made up to show what a credit union website built with Raytha can look like. The rates, people and places are invented.
